research_rationale: EO 13243 (66 FR 66262) of December 18, 2001 provides an order of succession within the Department of Housing and Urban Development. Sec. 3, which supersedes Secs. 1 and 2 of Executive Order 14109, is a one-time supersession performed on the order's effective date of 2025-09-30; the other thirty-one clauses are the continuance, the allocation of functions, the effective-date provision and the general provisions, whose only own-terms end (2027-09-30) is after the cutoff. No held instrument amends or revokes the order, and the bounded searches found only citations, so those clauses are carried as operative through 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No savings or residual-effects clause appears in the order; Sec. 5(a) is a construction rule preserving agency and OMB authority. The supersession of Executive Order 14109 Secs. 1 and 2 is recorded as performed on 2025-09-30. No held later instrument transfers or preserves rights under the order, and the bounded searches found no savings issue.

research_rationale: EO 12879 (58 FR 59929) of November 8, 1993 fixes the order of succession of officers to act as Secretary of the Navy. The held original (two Federal Register pages) was read in full and confirmed to be the order (number, date and subject agree with the register row). The eleven clauses cover the whole text; none has an own-terms end, no held later instrument amends, revokes or supersedes the order, and the three bounded searches found no ending statement. All clauses are carried as operative through 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No savings or residual-effects clause appears in the order. Sec. 2 states that succession does not vacate the successor's statutory appointment, which is a standing limit and not a savings clause. No held later instrument amends, revokes or supersedes the order, so nothing is transferred or accrued under a later instrument.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts that cite the order by number (none beyond the original and the 1989 OFR codification note in the registered set) and the three bounded searches, which returned citation hits only. The order's own wording has no until, expire, terminate or condition language that ends any section; the only duration language in Sec. 1(b)(1) limits each acting designation to the Secretary's absence or disability.
scope_check: Eleven clauses (Sec. 1(a) with items (1) to (4), Sec. 1(b) with items (1) and (2), Sec. 1(c), Sec. 1(d) and Sec. 2) cover the whole text; Sec. 1(a) is carried as the scope sec1 together with its lead-in.
independent_command_check: Each item is a standing succession rule, tie-break, exception or interim-basis provision. None is a one-time command with a performance date, none depends on another having been performed, and none has an end date, so no clause ended earlier than the order as a whole.
savings_check: No savings or residual-effects clause appears in the order. Sec. 2 states that succession does not vacate the successor's statutory appointment, which is a standing limit and not a savings clause. No held later instrument amends, revokes or supersedes the order, so nothing is transferred or accrued under a later instrument.
